title: How do you make capsule art and trailers with AI that don't look like slop?
author: Dramatic-Dust-9413
selftext:
Solo dev here, Claude writes my code.   
  
Last week I spent a whole day on the Steam capsule for my game, trying to keep it from looking like AI slop.

I didn't want to use ChatGPT or Midjourney for it. Everything in the game is drawn by code from vector shapes, and a generated image would have looked like a different game. Players also spot that look instantly and I didn't want the first thing they see to make them scroll past.

What I ended up doing: no image generator. I built the scene in Claude Design and then had Claude port it to code, so the final art is drawn on a canvas from vector paths, gradients and masks. For the trailer I recorded the actual game frame by frame with the clock fast forwarded.

The result is good, but not great.

So how do you handle this?

https://i.redd.it/oranicueqkyh1.png

\- Do you use AI for key art at all, or is that the one thing you pay an artist for?

\- If you use image generators, how do you keep the style consistent with the actual game?

\- For trailers, what made the biggest difference for you? Editing, pacing, music, something else?



If you have thoughts on mine, I'm listening. Sheers :)

comments.author: Dramatic-Dust-9413
comments.body:
Really valuable input, thanks for taking the time to look that closely.  
  
I’ll keep experimenting with other ways to make it feel less shape-y. Honest question though: do you think vector art like this can get much more organic, or is that clean look just part of the deal?

replies.author: Shalke97
replies.body: You can try telling Claude exactly that and See what he comes Up with! Maybe He knows a solution. I rarely use Claude for graphics. And so far almost only in 3D, where it is also lacking . Thats why my released Game Grim Reach Idle is mostly UI as an idler

replies.author: Dramatic-Dust-9413
replies.body:
The improvement from this conversation is already crazy:

https://i.redd.it/eiivwynqslyh1.png

comments.author: shaymagen
comments.body: Since everything in your game is code-drawn vectors, I'd honestly keep that approach for the capsule and just push the composition: one big readable focal object, the title much larger, and always check it at the tiny size most people actually see it. For the trailer, getting to the first exciting moment in the first 2-3 seconds usually matters way more than music or fancy editing.
